summary: Renders a text string through TextRenderToSurface and, when the measured width (*a3) exceeds the caller's limit a2, truncates the string by nulling trailing characters one at a time and re-measuring until the width fits or the string is fully consumed. Returns 0 when the string is NULL, otherwise the last measured result (which is 0 when the string eventually fits or is emptied).

local_names.this: render surface object whose text buffer is measured by TextRenderToSurface
local_names.a2: maximum allowed rendered width; the truncation target
local_names.a3: in/out pointer to the rendered width; also the string pointer used for re-measurement after truncation
local_names.v4: original text string pointer preserved across truncation
local_names.v7: cursor walking backward from the end of the string, nulling one character at a time
local_names.v8: char copy of a4 forwarded as the resolve flag on each re-measure
local_names.v9: rendered height output pointer shared across measurements

operations.description: Guard: all work happens only when the input string a3 is non-NULL; otherwise the function returns the initial result 0.
Initializes result to 0 and v4 to the input string a3 before the guard.
When the string is present, resets the output pointers: a3 is set to 0 (via the local copy) and v9 to 0 before measurement.
First measurement: TextRenderToSurface(this, v4, &a3, &v9, a4) computes the rendered width into a3 and height into v9.
Sets result to a2 (the width limit) as the default return after the first measurement.
Guard: enters the truncation loop only when the measured width (int)a3 is greater than the limit a2.
Computes v7 = &v4[strlen(v4) + 1], a pointer one past the string's NUL terminator, as the starting point of backward truncation.

Truncation loop: while the measured width still exceeds a2, decrement v7, null the character now at v7 (removing one trailing character), and re-measure via TextRenderToSurface(this, v4, &a3, &v9, v8). The loop breaks early when v7 walks back to the start of the string (v4 == v7), so an emptied string also terminates the loop.
Returns result: 0 when the input string was NULL or the final measurement fits, otherwise the value of the last re-measurement.
